name: Sori
confidence_why: The only description of Sori stress is Blust 2021, a sketch written up from two days of 1975 elicitation with a single teenage speaker, in which Blust calls stress "the most problematic feature" of his data, records penultimate as the apparent default alongside antepenultimate and final forms, tentatively concludes that stress is variable and non-phonemic, and says the matter "clearly deserves further consideration"; Ross 1988 says nothing about Sori stress and no other source exists.
catalog_citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Sketch 4: Sori. In: Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, LLM Special Issue 2021 (Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea, ISSN 0023-1959), pp. 235ff. PDF from langlxmelanesia.com.
catalog_quote: The most problematic feature of the vowels in my data on Sori concerns stress, which was intially recorded as penultimate. This pattern seems to represent the default case in the language, but some forms were recorded with antepenultimate or final stress, as with [bárawiɁ] ‘trivet, three stones of the hearth’, [báhawaj] ‘sugarcane’, [mwíhinoŋ] ‘stern of a canoe’, or [mbruwéj] ‘crocodile’, [uhúɁ] ‘cough’, [hotów] ‘hiccup’. However, apparent stress contrasts as in saŋóp ‘ten’ vs. húŋop ‘twenty’ suggest that stress is variable, and I therefore tentatively conclude that Sori does not have phonemic stress. Another indication that this probably is the correct analysis is that the three speakers of Lindrou with whom I worked were insistent on the placement of stress in their language, whereas the single speaker of Sori was not. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim at the stated place (p. 238, sec. 4.2) in the PDF we hold/text. (2) The deciding source is the only description of the language that exists: a 2021 sketch by Blust from 1975 fieldnotes (two days, one teenage speaker). Glottolog 5.1 has zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries for sori1242 besides it; Ross 1988 (downloaded and a full-text search for stress/accent) is silent on Sori stress; So the best available source is held and quoted. (3) The classification variable follows Blust's own words ('stress is variable.. tentatively conclude that Sori does not have phonemic stress'), with the hedged penultimate default recorded in the primary-stress rule; a check and B already logged the defensible alternatives (hedged fixed-penultimate or not determinable). sources.citation: Blust, Robert (researcher, depositor). 2014 [field data collected Feb-Apr 1975]. RB2-011: language packets keyed to a Tok Pisin master sheet (modified Swadesh list and grammatical items) for 28 Admiralty Islands languages; Sori on pp. 296-308, speaker Gaspar Francis. Blust Field Notebooks collection, Kaipuleohone, University of Hawai'i Digital Language Archive (ScholarSpace). hdl:10125/33171. Scanned JPGs in five zip files (RB2-011-01.05, 79-118 MB each).

sources.note: Raw elicitation sheets (wordlist + grammatical items) in phonetic transcription; no analytic tone statement expected. Relevant as the primary transcription data behind Blust 2021, whose sketch reports variable, non-phonemic stress and (per our catalog entry) does not mention tone; the sheets may show whether Blust marked stress/pitch on individual forms.
